source._php_version_note: WordPress 7.1.4 requires PHP >= 7.4 (wp-includes/version.php $required_php_version) and its readme.html recommends 8.3+; the SQLite plugin supports PHP 7.2+. Since 2026-10-10 the image runs Ubuntu 24.04's own PHP 8.3 (it reports 8.3.6; Ubuntu backports security fixes into it) instead of the official php:8.4-apache-bookworm image, whose Debian 12 base our cerodeo-v1 scan grades F on vulnerabilities Debian does not fix. PHP 8.4 on Ubuntu 24.04 would need a third-party archive (a PPA): a supply-chain decision, not taken here; preflight check_php BLOCKs a retarget whose source needs more than the image's PHP.
source._ext_note: docker-library/wordpress installs bcmath exif gd(avif,freetype,jpeg,webp) intl mysqli zip + pecl imagick. This kit keeps all of them except imagick and gd's AVIF, from Ubuntu's packages (runtime_packages): php8.3-gd (Ubuntu's libgd3: freetype, jpeg, png, gif, webp; gd_info() reports no AVIF), -intl, -zip, -bcmath, -mysql (mysqli for the optional MySQL/MariaDB mode, mysqlnd, no client library; the package also carries pdo_mysql), -sqlite3 (pdo_sqlite, what the SQLite drop-in needs), -curl, -mbstring, -xml; exif and fileinfo with php8.3-common, opcache and sodium with php8.3-cli. source.php_extensions is what the build asserts is loaded in both the Apache and the CLI configuration; post_copy_run still checks php -m and a warning-free PHP start.
source.submodule_init_cmd: git clone --depth 1 --branch v3.0.2 -q https://github.com/WordPress/sqlite-database-integration /tmp/sqlite-src && test "$(git -C /tmp/sqlite-src rev-parse HEAD)" = 085ea60b16c648d40464654afa667f0812c040de && mkdir -p /src/readystack-vendor && cp -R /tmp/sqlite-src/packages/plugin-sqlite-database-integration /src/readystack-vendor/sqlite-database-integration && rm /src/readystack-vendor/sqlite-database-integration/wp-includes/database && cp -R /tmp/sqlite-src/packages/mysql-on-sqlite/src /src/readystack-vendor/sqlite-database-integration/wp-includes/database && rm -f /src/readystack-vendor/sqlite-database-integration/composer.json && test -f /src/readystack-vendor/sqlite-database-integration/wp-includes/database/version.php && rm -rf /tmp/sqlite-src
source._submodule_init_note: WordPress has no submodules; this is the renderer's post-clone hook (RUN after `git clone`, in /src, online). It vendors WordPress.org's SQLite Database Integration at tag v3.0.2, refusing anything but commit 085ea60b16c648d40464654afa667f0812c040de (tags can move), and assembles the plugin the way upstream's bin/build-sqlite-plugin-zip.sh does. NOT touched by scripts/retarget.py: bump tag + commit here (and sqlite_integration below) by hand when a newer plugin release is needed.
source._prune_note: The 12 older default themes are not in the wordpress.org 7.1.2 download (only Twenty Twenty-Three/Four/Five are); pruning them makes the shipped wp-content match the release minus Akismet. twentytwentyfive's package.json/package-lock.json are the theme's CSS build manifests (118 dev-only npm packages: postcss/cssnano/browserslist), not runtime code; removed so no SBOM tool catalogues an npm tree that is not installed.
source._app_copies_note: ENUMERATED (the nextcloud pattern), not '.': the WordPress root files + wp-admin + wp-includes go to the docroot /var/www/html; wp-content goes to /usr/src/wordpress/wp-content as the pristine seed the entrypoint copies into an empty volume; the assembled SQLite plugin goes outside the docroot. readme.html and license.txt ship as in the release; wp-config-sample.php does not (the image ships wp-config.php). If a future WordPress adds a root-level file, add it here (a missing src fails the COPY loudly; an unlisted new file would be silently absent).
